hints.title: Pair Difference Analysis
hints.text: For each symmetrical pair, changing zero numbers preserves their current difference. Changing one number can produce any difference up to a pair-specific upper bound.

hints.title: Change Cost Ranges
hints.text: For a candidate target difference X: zero changes if X equals current difference, one change if X is within the single-element ceiling, and two changes if X exceeds it.

hints.title: Range Addition Sweep
hints.text: Record the change cost transitions using a difference array across difference values from zero to k. Prefix sum sweeps through all targets in linear time.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minChanges(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        diff = [0] * (k + 2)
        for i in range(n // 2):
            a, b = nums[i], nums[n - 1 - i]
            d = abs(a - b)
            m = max(a, b, k - a, k - b)
            diff[0] += 1
            diff[d] -= 1
            diff[d + 1] += 1
            diff[m + 1] += 1
        
        curr = 0
        min_changes = float('inf')
        for x in range(k + 1):
            curr += diff[x]
            if curr < min_changes:
                min_changes = curr
        return min_changes
```

complexity.notes: Single pass to populate difference boundaries followed by linear prefix sum scan.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating each possible difference X from zero to k individually takes O(n * k) which times out.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Difference array of size k + 2 achieves optimal linear runtime.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Models cost intervals with range difference updates and computes global optimum.
